title: The Safety of Hand Surgery in the Anticoagulated Patient
brief_summary: If operating on the anticoagulated patient has been safe for one of the investigators' surgeons for the past 10 years then providing prospective data that substantiates this could prevent complications related to the discontinuation of anticoagulation for hand surgery patients in the future.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults over 18 years of age
* Taking daily anti-coagulant medication
* Having hand or wrist surgery

Exclusion Criteria:

* Surgery proximal to wrist
* Pregnant females
* INR \> 3.5
study_population: Adults over 18 years of age having hand surgery while on anti-coagulant medication. Control subjects undergoing hand and wrist surgery without anticoagulant medications will be enrolled if they are over 18 years of age and able to consent to research participation. Patients on Coumadin with INR values less than or equal to 3.5 will be eligible for study inclusion.
